sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Interactive Language Education and Automated Tutoring Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state corporate tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law foundation with Common Law-influenced corporate and commercial statutes, notably Ley 32 de 1927 on Sociedades Anónimas)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 31 Oct 2012, covering investment and digital trade)
Panama-Spain BIT (in force 2003) and Panama-Spain DTA (in force 2011)
Panama-Netherlands BIT (in force 2001) and Panama-Netherlands DTA (in force 2011)
Panama-UAE DTA (in force 2012), Panama-Qatar DTA (in force 2013), Panama-Korea DTA (in force 2021)
WTO/GATS commitments applicable to electronically supplied educational services

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley No. 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT regime, last amended by Ley 197 de 2021); Ley No. 254 de 29 de diciembre de 2023 creating the Registro de Titularidad Final administered by the Dirección General de Sujetos No Financieros (DGSNF); Ley 32 de 1927 (Sociedades Anónimas) as amended by Ley 5 de 2011; FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 22 and 24 apply; Panama was re-listed on the FATF grey list on 21 February 2025, accelerating enforcement of UBO and reporting obligations.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access — the beneficial ownership register is not open to the general public; access is granted to DGSNF, Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF), Public Registry, and foreign competent authorities under AEOI and treaty exchange mechanisms; bearer shares are prohibited and existing bearer securities must be immobilized with a licensed central custodian.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the Escritura Pública de Constitución (notarial deed of incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notaría Pública del Primer Circuito, Panama City
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic certification by the Public Registry for Panamanian use; Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs only when the deed is later submitted to foreign authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity documentation (passport or national ID) of each shareholder, director, corporate officer and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing national authority (passport office or civil registry) plus notarization by a notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague member states; Consular Legalization before the Panamanian Consulate for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency, certificate of good standing and constitutive documents of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or licensed registered agent in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague member states; Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter concerning source of funds and banking history of the incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution (correspondent or home-country bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer, supplemented by Hague Apostille or consular legalization where the resident agent's KYC policy so requires

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors, officers and UBOs against (i) the national PEP register and foreign-PEP databases per FATF Recommendation 12, (ii) OFAC SDN List, (iii) UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, and (iv) EU restrictive measures; enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth analysis is triggered where any UBO holds at least 10% or where screening reveals adverse media; screening results must be documented, dated and re-run within 90 days prior to notarization of the incorporation deed; suspicious transaction reports are filed with the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá — online filing portal (Sistema de Trámites en Línea / SIPE) at www.registro-publico.gob.pa — name clearance obtained via the Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre (vista de nombre) procedure
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Registry proceedings are conducted in Spanish; names must be entered in Latin script and must end with 'Sociedad Anónima' or the abbreviation 'S.A.'; foreign-language denominations are acceptable provided a Spanish transliteration or translation is recorded; the name must be distinguishable from all existing registrations and must not be misleading as to activity or nationality.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANCO, BANK, FINANCIERA, FINANCIAL — requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Bancos
SEGURO, REASEGURO, INSURANCE — requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia de Seguros
FONDO DE INVERSIÓN, VALORES, BOLSA, TRUST, FIDEICOMISO — requires prior authorization of the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores
NACIONAL, OFICIAL, GOBIERNO, ESTADO, REPÚBLICA, MUNICIPAL — requires prior ministerial or State-entity authorization
LICOR, ALCOHOL, TABACO, SALUD, CLÍNICA — requires sectoral health licensing
CRUZ ROJA, CÁMARA DE COMERCIO, and names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company are absolutely prohibited
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name reservation is valid for 30 calendar days; no statutory extension exists and lapse requires a new application with a fresh search fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) re-file alternative candidate names immediately, or (ii) file a formal administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) with the Dirección General del Registro Público within 10 business days under Ley 38 de 2000, followed by judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia; in practice, name conflicts are efficiently cured by submitting new candidates in the same application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for the proposed EdTech business: the S.A. must maintain a registered office at the premises of its licensed resident agent in Panama, and no physical branch, local staff or server presence is legally required where operations and digital tutoring services are supplied from abroad; documentary substance (board minutes, accounting records, bank account, UBO filings) remains critical for treaty access and commercial banking.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (estimated 5%) for a low-risk EdTech S.A. because DGSNF conducts unannounced inspections primarily at the resident agent's office; Public Registry physical verification is triggered only upon irregular filings or complaints; however, a documented inspection trail (proper corporate minutes, shareholder registry, accounting books kept in Spanish or English) will reduce risk to negligible.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search and reservation (Certificado de Búsqueda de Nombre)
Notarization of the Escritura Pública de Constitución before a First Circuit Notary Public
Registry inscription of the Sociedad Anónima in the Mercantile Section (derecho de inscripción)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory sliding-scale registration fee based on the stated USD 10,000 capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified copies of the incorporation deed and registration certificate
Resident agent and registered office service — first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed resident agent (law firm or authorized agency)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalization of incorporation deed and KYC documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores (Dirección de Autenticaciones) or foreign apostille authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille and consular fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUC/NIT tax registration (inscripción en el Registro Único de Contribuyentes)
Beneficial ownership registry sworn filing (declaración jurada de titularidad final)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Sujetos No Financieros (DGSNF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing fee assessed under Ley 254 de 2023

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal and certified Spanish translation of any non-Spanish KYC or corporate instruments

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Panama Law 32 of 1927), as amended and codified, especially Articles 1-10, 18, 30-45; Executive Decree 4 of 2016 on Mercantile Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantile Section), through a registered Panamanian attorney or notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima), registered as an inscription in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No mandatory paid-up capital in escrow. The Sociedad Anónima must have authorized capital of at least US$10,000 or its equivalent; the incorporators may subscribe and issue a minimal paid-up share. No escrow account or capital deposit rule applies to an ordinary EdTech S.A.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation approves and ratifies the share subscription for the full authorized capital as recorded in the Deed of Incorporation, without requiring paid-in capital in excess of the statutory minimum. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the corporation shall be the address shown in the Public Registry, that changes to this address must be adopted by board resolution, and that the resident agent is retained to receive service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following persons are appointed as President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to hold office for one year or until successors are elected, and the President is authorized to execute banking, commercial, and regulatory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama Notary Public (Notario de Circuito) and Registro Público de Panamá online name-reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search and reserve the proposed corporate name through the Registro Público de Panamá name-reservation system. Upon name approval, at least two incorporators, or the resident agent with sufficient power, must appear before a Panamanian notary to execute the Escritura Pública de Constitución. The deed must state the corporate name, domicile, object, capital structure, classes of shares, number of directors, registered agent, and initial officers.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Reserva de Nombre issued by Registro Público
Draft Spanish-language public deed of incorporation
Notarized copies of passports or identity documents of incorporators
Proposed by-laws and text of the first provisional resolutions
Resident agent acceptance and appointment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is denied due to similarity, apply for a new name and re-execute the deed. If the notary identifies a deficiency in required clauses, correct the deed by supplementary act before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the public deed in the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección de Personas Jurídicas / Mercantile Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized original public deed with the Public Registry, together with the corresponding application and proof of payment of registration tariffs. The Registry will examine the deed against mandatory legal clauses and, if compliant, issue the inscription certificate that gives the Sociedad Anónima its formal legal personality and date of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Original notarized public deed with notary certification
Legalized certificate of name reservation
Signed cover letter or filing application from the resident agent
Proof of payment of government filing fees
Certified copy of the resident agent appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a razon de rechazo or notice of deficiencies, the filing attorney may cure the observations within the statutory period by filing a supplementary public deed, clarificatory document, or amended article, and then refile the inscription within the Registry's administrative cure window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold first board meeting, adopt governance resolutions, and legalize statutory corporate books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered office of the corporation, resident agent, and Panamanian notary for book legalization
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the board of directors, either in person or virtually, and adopt the first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office, and officer appointments. The corporate secretary must prepare the share register, minutes book, and share certificate records. These books are then legalized or stamped by the appropriate registry or notarial authority as required for Panamanian companies.
required_dossiers: Minutes of the first board meeting
Share subscription and issuance records
Share register book
Corporate minutes book
Stock certificate stubs and specimen certificates
Registered agent confirmation of office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Public Registry or notary rejects legalization of the books due to formatting or missing pages, correct the book entry format, ensure sequential page numbering, and resubmit with the applicable refiling fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain municipal operating notice and complete employer registration and administrative filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía de Panamá or corresponding municipality, Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), and Caja de Seguro Social (CSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file the Aviso de Operación with the municipal authority at the company's business address. For a virtual EdTech operation without a physical office, provide a declaration of digital-only activity. In parallel, register the company with the DGI for its Employer Identification Number if not yet assigned, and register as an employer with CSS within 30 days of hiring any employee.
required_dossiers: Registro Público inscription certificate
Company RUC or DGI application
Aviso de Operación form
Lease contract or declaration of virtual-only office
Identity documents of the legal representative and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality observes a discrepancy in business address or activity, submit the corrected declaration and pay any minor administrative fee. If the DGI or CSS queries classification, provide the ISIC 6201 and NAICS 611710 activity description and update the employer registration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI), Dirección General de Industrias, and municipal licensing office
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (municipal operation notice) - not a mandatory manufacturing license; required only as a light registration if a physical office or tenancy exists.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Dirección de Verificación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 - Exempt / Registration not required for pure-software EdTech services with no physical production facility.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial point-source wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste expected. Any future physical office must comply with municipal wastewater regulations and general office waste disposal requirements under MiAMBIENTE's administrative guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a virtual-only EdTech operation. If the company later opens a physical office or tutoring center, it must obtain a fire-safety certificate from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, a structural occupancy inspection from the local municipality, and an occupational health workplace registration with the Caja de Seguro Social and Ministerio de Salud.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama; online portals: DGI Sede Electrónica (https://sede.mef.gob.pa), DGI institutional portal (https://www.dgi.mef.gob.pa), SFE e-invoicing system (https://sfe.dgi.mef.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the newly incorporated Panamanian Sociedad Anónima (PA_CORP), the registration workflow is: (1) complete public-registry inscription at the Registro Público keeping the registered agent; (2) the legal representative or the fiduciary files the DGI RUC application (Formulario RUC-1) accompanied by the articles of incorporation, certificado de registro, domicile certificate, and a sworn statement of economic activity (ISIC 6201; digital EdTech services); (3) a Panamanian Contador Público Autorizado (CPA) must certify the registration; (4) obtain the municipal Aviso de Operación (business license) in the district of the registered address; (5) activate digital credentials at the Sede Electrónica and register in the SFE e-invoicing module; (6) for foreign-owner identification, shareholders' passports or entity documents must be filed for the Registro de Beneficiario Final under AML Law 23 of 2015. A foreign entity without a local S.A. does not obtain a Panamanian RUC unless it maintains a permanent establishment in Panama; no threshold-based VAT registration exists, so every taxable operator must register regardless of turnover, while the USD 36,024 threshold only elects the Pequeño Contribuyente simplified regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a check-the-box, LLC-transparent, or hybrid-mismatch election: an S.A. is mandatorily a corporation taxed at entity level (ISR 25%) and as an ITBMS taxpayer on Panamanian-source income only. Available statutory elections: (i) Pequeño Contribuyente regime under Law 82 of 2011 for annual gross revenue not exceeding USD 36,024, paying a final 3% gross-receipts tax in lieu of ISR and ITBMS; (ii) quarterly ISR/ITBMS filing election for taxpayers with annual gross revenue below USD 300,000; (iii) for EdTech export income, the taxpayer may issue invoices as 'no causado' (0% ITBMS) when the service is supplied to Apple/Google non-resident marketplaces and exploited abroad; where ITBMS has been charged in error on export revenue, the taxpayer elects the refund or credit mechanism under the Fiscal Code; (iv) exporters may elect to accumulate and offset input ITBMS credits under the export reimbursement regime against their periodic ITBMS declarations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) – Panamanian value-added tax; territorial and destination-based
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No exemption or de minimis threshold: any person habitually engaged in the transfer of chattel goods or the provision of services on Panamanian territory is obliged to register for ITBMS (Código Fiscal, Article 1061 et seq.); the only quantitative demarcation is the elective small-taxpayer line of B/.36,024.00 (USD 36,024.00) annual gross revenue, below which the 3% Pequeño Contribuyente gross tax may substitute for ITBMS; subscription digital services sold to final consumers in Panama remain taxable at 7% even when delivered electronically.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time clearance under the DGI 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica' (SFE) based on Law 95 of 2018 and the applicable DGI resolutions. All ITBMS-registered taxpayers, including EdTech ISIC 6201 providers, must issue XML electronic invoices in the SFE with DGI real-time validation: each invoice is transmitted immediately via DGI web services/API, and upon validation receives a unique DGI authorization code and a QR code printed on the PDF or customer copy. Paper or point-of-sale invoices are permitted only under SFE contingency mode (platform unavailability), and the contingency batch must be uploaded to the DGI within the deadline fixed by DGI resolutions, generally within 48 hours after restoration. The system also obliges digital emitters to accept electronic credit and debit notes, to issue e-invoices for each Apple IAP or Google Play Billing settlement as a B2B export sale, and to file periodic ITBMS returns electronically through the Sede Electrónica with automatic cross-matching of authorized invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export supplies are outside the territorial incidence of ITBMS ('no causado', effective 0%): (1) goods: merchandise must be physically removed from Panama and exported through the DUA export declaration in the SIGA customs system; (2) services and digital subscriptions: the service is supplied to Apple/Google marketplaces as non-resident resellers or directly to non-resident users, and the software use and exploitation occurs outside Panamanian territory; the taxpayer must document the foreign residence of the platform or customer, the offshore application usage, and the foreign-platform settlement proceeds. Eligibility is substantiated at invoicing time: the exporter must issue an SFE export invoice conspicuously marked 'Exportación – ITBMS no causado' and must retain proof of non-resident status of the buyer (Apple/Google legal-entity certificates, foreign IP addresses, user geolocation, platform seller reports). Input ITBMS borne on costs attributable to exports is creditable or refundable under the export reimbursement mechanism of the Fiscal Code.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Declaración Única Aduanera) filed in the SIGA customs clearance system with operative exit confirmation, required for goods exported as physical media.

Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing dispatch of exported goods for physical exports; for pure digital exports through Apple IAP or Google Play Billing, the SFE export invoice, the platform settlement report, and the digital-content distribution agreement.
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank settlement statement (SWIFT credit advice, Apple/Google payout statement) evidencing the receipt of export proceeds before the applicable repatriation benchmark.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI audit directorate (Dirección de Fiscalización) cross-checks SFE export invoices, SIGA customs outflows, and bank receipts of proceeds: invoices for services in fact consumed in Panama, or lacking evidence of foreign exploitation, are reclassified as local taxable supplies. Consequences include: reassessment of the omitted 7% ITBMS plus monthly surcharge and interest; fines of one to three times the evaded tax (Código Fiscal, Articles 760-761); professional sanctions against the certifying CPA; withdrawal of the SFE emitter authorization; re-opening of prior fiscal years within the five-year statute of limitations in cases of fraudulent concealment; criminal tax evasion exposure under Law 114 of 2004 with imprisonment of two to five years where the tax loss exceeds USD 36,024; and bank AML downgrades or suspension under Law 23 of 2015. Panama has no statutory FX repatriation deadline because the US dollar is legal tender; the 180-day benchmark is the monitoring convention used by DGI audits and AML/CFT reviews to test whether export proceeds were genuinely realized and traceable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). Panama does not have an issuing central bank; the U.S. dollar is the sole legal tender under Decree-Law 4 of 2012 and the Monetary Agreement with the United States. The SBP supervises all banking activity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. Panama is a dollarized jurisdiction with no exchange control regime and no separate legal tender. Capital and current account transactions are free of any prior authorization or divestment restrictions. There is no statutory limitation on the repatriation of dividends, interest, or capital; the only practical requirements are standard AML/KYC verification by the banking intermediary and, for cash transactions above USD 10,000, reporting to the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement exists. Since Panama has no central bank and no foreign exchange control authority, export receipts (including EdTech subscription revenue from Apple and Google) are not subject to any surrender, conversion, or mandatory holding period. All receipts may be freely retained, reinvested, or remitted abroad.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Capital contributions can be received after KYC approval)
Operational Account (state-owned; less focused on offshore non-resident structures)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low-to-Medium as a primary liquidity rail, Medium as a supplementary rail. Panama's SBP does not authorize offshore digital EMIs (e-money institutions) to provide deposit-taking or corporate payment clearing without a full Panamanian banking license. EMIs incorporated in third-country jurisdictions may operate only through a domestic partner bank's omnibus accounts and cannot directly access Panama's clearing infrastructure or settlement accounts. For the EdTech subscription enterprise, a regulated Panamanian bank account is mandatory as the main clearing account; offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex) may only be used for low-value outbound payouts to independent language tutors or to facilitate vendor remittances in non-USD currencies. Legal constraints: Operation of an EMI without a local license may violate the Panamanian Commercial Code and Banking Law; the company must ensure that any EMI partner does not solicit 'banking clients' in Panama and that the EMI's cross-border payment services are conducted through a licensed correspondent bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandate: In-person appearance of at least one director or beneficial owner is the near-universal market standard in Panama. The SBP's Customer Due Diligence Rules (Accord 1-2014, as amended by Accords 7-2016 and 4-2020) require banks to identify and verify natural persons, which in practice entails physical authentication of the passport and a standard banker's interview. A minority of private banks offer 'remote onboarding' for non-resident investors, subject to independent verification by a qualified intermediary, video call, and final approval by the bank's compliance committee; this is not a statutory right and is never guaranteed. For a non-resident owned EdTech S.A., we strongly recommend that at least one authorized director physically attend the onboarding meeting at the chosen tier-1 bank in Panama City to eliminate institutional friction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is not physically present and the account is intended to concentrate revenues from global app stores without an evident local business substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legalised shareholders' and directors' certificates issued by the Panamanian Public Registry; notarized and apostilled passports; a professional investor bank reference letter from the presenting bank in the owner's jurisdiction; a signed corporate organizational chart; audited (or internally prepared) financial statements showing active subscription operations; a service agreement with a licensed Panamanian resident agent (fiduciary) evidencing management oversight.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring micropayments from Apple and Google with no documentary link to a bona fide EdTech language-learning business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple Developer Program contract and Google Play Console merchant agreement; merchant IDs and digital product lists downloaded directly from the platforms to show recurring subscription activity; a weekly transaction report coupled to a CRM-generated user activity log; user privacy and refund policies compliant with Panamanian Law 81 of 2019 on personal data; an independent accounting review of the revenue recognition methodology.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consolidation of subscription revenue and periodic payments to freelance language tutors across multiple jurisdictions that may be perceived as unlicensed remittance activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed vendor onboarding file containing contracts, tax identification numbers, and employment verification; a formally adopted treasury policy manual regulating disbursement thresholds and approvals; a board-approved cap table and dividend distribution policy; a written legal opinion confirming that the EdTech platform does not require a Panamanian remittance or payment-processing license.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: use bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's account with (i) the corporate name, (ii) the Panamanian Registro Público identification number (F-), (iii) reference 'Share Capital Contribution' or 'Paid-in Capital', and (iv) the shareholder's KYC documentation. No central bank permit is required. The receiving bank requires an updated Public Registry certification, a board resolution approving the capital issuance, and a sworn declaration of source of funds. For amounts above USD 10,000, the bank must file a transaction record with the UAF; approval is immediate with no governmental delay.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EdTech software supplier and infrastructure payments, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for payables up to USD 500,000. For larger structured intellectual-property licensing agreements, an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit (confirmed by a top-50 U.S. or European bank) is the standard mechanism. Domestic clearing uses Panama's automated clearing house (SITI) and international transfers move through New York correspondent banks. Apple and Google payouts are remitted by the app stores to the Panama S.A. USD account using their own settlement channels, which are not subject to Panamanian clearing taxes or additional reporting beyond standard bank statement accrual.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (USD/COP, USD/BRL, USD/MXN, USD/EUR) executed with licensed Panamanian banks or international brokers registered with the SBP.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for regional emerging-market currency exposures, with settlement in USD and no physical delivery in Panama.
Cross-currency swaps (USD against EUR or LATAM currencies) for intercompany loan hedging and invoice matching.
Plain-vanilla FX call and put options to hedge vendor costs and subscription scaling risks.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax (Tarifa Anual) of the Panama S.A. and confirmation of legal standing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) through authorized local banks; enforcement coordination with Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to January 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalties: USD 100 if paid in February, USD 250 in March, USD 500 in April; failure to pay for six consecutive months triggers administrative strike-off of the S.A., followed by automatic dissolution after an additional six months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Legal Agent Due Diligence Report (Reporte Anual de Actualización de Datos) confirming registered office, directors, officers, and shareholding data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (General Registry of Legal Entities), submitted exclusively by the appointed resident legal agent (abogado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 1 to July 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing restricts issuance of registry certifications and judicial/administrative certificates; Registro Público may impose fines up to USD 100 and repeated omission is a ground for administrative strike-off proceedings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Panama S.A. not listed, not licensed, and with annual gross worldwide income below USD 1,000,000 is exempt from mandatory independent audit; statutory audit by a licensed CPA is required if annual gross income exceeds USD 1,000,000, if the S.A. is regulated (banking, insurance, finance), or if the DGI requests audited financial statements based on revenue or asset size
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama (NIIF) for general-purpose financial statements; small and non-public entities may apply IFRS for SMEs where turnover is below the audit threshold; territorial-source basis applies for income tax

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident legal agent must collect and keep current beneficial ownership information under AML/due diligence rules; annually, the agent obtains a signed declaration confirming that no unnotified share transfers have occurred and that the UBO schedule remains accurate. UBO data is not made public but must be produced to the Financial Intelligence Unit or DGI upon valid request within 72 hours

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,000 per annum depending on the registered agent and service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - USD 3,000 per annum when an independent audit is required; generally not incurred below the compulsory audit threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday; territorial taxation may exempt foreign-source subscription revenue if the EdTech functions, assets and risks are located outside Panama. Optional negotiated incentives may apply only under the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime or City of Knowledge, not routine S.A. operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 193 (Declaración de Impuesto sobre la Renta de Personas Jurídicas / Informative Income Tax Return), filed through DGI e-Tax 2.0 electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; taxpayers also make quarterly prepayments (anticipos) to DGI
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return due within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity name, RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), and stated juridical domicile.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the S.A.'s Panama RUC and registered agent address; no personal identification of non-resident owners is included in this box.
Enter ISIC 6201 for computer programming and related EdTech subscription activities; if the S.A. merely invoices through app stores, consider whether active revenue characterization is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue derived from sources inside Panama plus other taxable Panama-source receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a territorial S.A., exclude gross proceeds from foreign subscribers' use of the language-learning app abroad; only include sales where the user is in Panama or the services are deemed utilized in Panama.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 530 - Cost of sales and allowable deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses necessary to generate taxable income, including app platform fees (Apple/Google), hosting, royalties, salaries and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses attributable to Panama-source revenue are deductible; allocate app-store commissions reasonably if a portion of revenue is non-Panamanian.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after NOL application and non-deductible items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply NOL carryforward (maximum five years) against taxable Panama-source income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) computed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No need to gross up for deemed distribution; this tax is before dividend tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly advance payments, withholding tax credits, and any foreign tax credit where a Panama-foreign tax treaty applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits formally receipted by DGI or documented in the electronic system; attach PDF evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box Final - Net tax payable or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay via Panama banking portal; refunds are processed administratively and may trigger substance review if refund is based on foreign-source losses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an extemporaneous declaration surcharge and monthly interest on the unpaid tax; under the Tax Code, failure to file or incorrect filing can draw fines plus 1% monthly late-payment interest. Persistent non-filing may cause the RUC to be suspended and the company to be sanctioned under anti-money laundering administrative rules.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% withholding on dividends distributed from taxed Panama-source profits; distributions sourced from foreign-source profits are generally not subject to Panama dividend tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a limited tax treaty network. To apply a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident shareholder must provide an annual Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) and submit a written relief request with the payer before distribution; the payer must retain the TRC and file an informational return with DGI. Without an in-force DTA, treaty relief is not available.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest remittances are generally not subject to Panama WHT. Royalties for use of technology/IP in Panama are Panama-source and are subject to 12.5% withholding if paid to a non-resident; treaty-protected royalties may be reduced or exempt under applicable DTA. For EdTech, this is relevant if the Panamanian S.A. licenses the app platform back to its foreign parent for use abroad — no Panama WHT should apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory transfer pricing documentation is expected when Panamanian gross revenue exceeds B/. 1,000,000 or related-party transactions exceed B/. 250,000 in a fiscal year; DGI may nonetheless require a Local File and Master File in any TP audit.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama applies a substance-over-form/territoriality doctrine for S.A. entities: foreign-source income characterization requires demonstrable offshore decision-making, active operation, personnel and bank accounts; passive collection of large platform revenues routed through Panama without local staff or offices is re-characterized as Panama-source trade or business, exposing the company to full 25% tax, penalties and director examinations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting Apple/Google Play commerce results, under-declaring Panama-source revenue, or fabricating NOL carryforwards to reduce taxable income to zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud (defraudación fiscal) that can be punished with imprisonment from 2 to 5 years, fines of ten to one hundred times the evaded annual income tax, and cancellation of tax registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns or direct underpricing may be jointly and severally liable for evaded tax plus interest; a criminal judge may impose travel bans (impedimento de salida) and asset embargoes during the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Panama S.A. with no offices, no employees, a nominee registered agent, and all decisions taken in the United States/China yet claiming complete territorial exemption for large EdTech revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI can disregard the invoicing entity, reclassify all revenue as Panama-source, assess 25% corporate tax plus default interest and a 10% extemporaneous return surcharge; amounts may be increased as 'non-deductible' distributions to shareholders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may be required to prove economic substance; failure exposes them to imposed deemed taxable income and civil restitution for corporate losses; intentional use of the shell to hide true ownership also triggers AML sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the S.A. as an undisclosed treasury vehicle, mixing subscription revenues without customer due diligence, or making opaque distributions to non-resident shareholders without beneficial ownership records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 23 of 2015 (as amended), fines from B/. 1 million for failure to maintain beneficial ownership records, and up to B/. 5 million for serious AML violations; commercial agents and resident agents can lose their licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be named in Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs); deliberate concealment of a politically exposed person or ultimate beneficial owner can lead to criminal prosecution, blacklisting on OFAC sanctions, travel bans and imprisonment.
